GITLAB_PROJECT_ID.description: Optional GitLab project id (or URL-encoded full path, e.g. mygroup%2Fmyrepo) to scope the import. When set, only that project's vulnerability_findings are imported via /api/v4/projects/{id}/vulnerability_findings. Omit to enumerate every project the token can see (via /api/v4/projects?membership=true) and import each one's findings.

GITLAB_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum severity floor (info | low | medium | high | critical). Filters out lower-severity findings both server-side (CSV-forwarded as the severity[] query parameter on /vulnerability_findings) and client-side after Faraday severity normalisation. Defaults to info (no filtering).

GITLAB_REPORT_TYPE.description: Optional GitLab Security Dashboard report type to scope the import — one of sast, dependency_scanning, container_scanning, secret_detection, dast, api_fuzzing, coverage_fuzzing. Forwarded as the report_type[] query parameter on /vulnerability_findings. Omit to import findings of every report type.

name: gitlab_security
title: GitLab Security Dashboard
description: GitLab Vulnerability Report REST API importer. Pulls security findings (SAST / dependency_scanning / container_scanning / secret_detection / DAST / API-fuzzing / coverage-fuzzing) from a GitLab instance and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. Lists projects via /api/v4/projects (or fetches a single project via /api/v4/projects/{id} when GITLAB_PROJECT_ID is set), then pulls per-project findings via /api/v4/projects/{id}/vulnerability_findings paginated with page / per_page. Each project becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because GitLab Security Dashboard findings live in source repos and merge-request diffs, not on IPs) with hostnames = project path_with_namespace; per-project findings attached as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per GitLab vulnerability_finding id with engine prefix derived from report_type ([SAST] / [SCA] / [CONTAINER] / [SECRETS] / [DAST] / [API-FUZZ] / [COV-FUZZ]), location summary (file:line for SAST / secret_detection, package@version for dependency_scanning, image+os for container_scanning, hostname+path for DAST), scanner name + confidence + project_fingerprint + state surfaced in the description; solution / remediation surfaced as Faraday resolution. Refs are split from GitLab's identifiers array — CVE-* identifiers populate the cve list (deduped, upper-cased), CWE-* / GHSA-* / OWASP / vendor rule ids populate refs; top-level links also surface as refs. Severity normalised from GitLab's bucket set (critical / high / medium / low / info / unknown — unknown collapses to info so the finding still imports), with CVSS v3 base_score fallback when only the cvss list / cvss3 dict is given; client-side GITLAB_MIN_SEVERITY floor enforced after normalisation, and the same floor CSV-forwarded as the severity[] query parameter. Status mapped from GitLab's state field (detected / confirmed → open, dismissed → risk-accepted, resolved → closed) with false_positive boolean and vulnerability_feedback feedback_type=dismissal as fallbacks. Auth: PRIVATE-TOKEN header carrying a GitLab personal / project / group access token with read_api scope; pre-built Bearer / OAuth / PRIVATE-TOKEN / JOB-TOKEN prefixes in the supplied value are detected and routed to the matching header. GITLAB_HOST is the GitLab base URL (e.g. https://gitlab.com or the self-hosted instance URL).
